title: MicroFitGut: a downstream microbiome analysis agent for Claude Code
description:
MicroFitGut is a Claude Code plugin for downstream analysis of 16S amplicon and shotgun metagenomic data. It takes a feature table — a phyloseq object, an ASV/taxonomy/metadata triplet, a MetaPhlAn or Kraken2 profile, or a PICRUSt2/HUMAnN functional table — through quality control, normalization, alpha and beta diversity, differential abundance, mixed and zero-inflated models, publication figures, and a reproducible report.

The design separates judgement from computation: a reference library of 16 documents encodes the analytical decisions (which normalization is valid for which test, which differential-abundance method suits which design, what every report must state), while 16 R modules comprising 222 functions perform the computation. Two auditing subagents check the result before publication.

MicroFitGut refuses combinations that produce clean but incorrect results: rarefied counts reaching DESeq2, UniFrac computed on a placeholder phylogeny, independent-samples tests applied to repeated measures, PERMANOVA conclusions unqualified by a dispersion check, and numbers in a report that do not trace to a logged artifact.

Benchmark mode scores a paper's stated claims rather than inferring agreement from taxon overlap: each claim is recorded in a machine-checkable form bound to the specific comparison it concerns, and a claim that cannot be scored blocks a clean "reproduced" verdict instead of being silently dropped.

The tool was validated by re-running the stated answers of a graduate microbiome course: 106 checks, 90 matching, with every difference attributed to a specific reproducible cause.
